text:
maya (pm): Quick idea: introduce a small "priority token" tier to handle predictable burst windows. Customers buy a subscription (priority-tier) + a bucket of tokens that convert into higher-priority routing for a percentage of requests. Want to align product + contract before spinning up infra work.

dan (sales): this could sell well to SMBs that hit periodic spikes. question: should tokens be per-tenant or per-route? customers ask per-route for product-level SLAs.

maya (pm): plan A: tokens are tenant-level but can be scoped to routes via billing tags. Plan B: per-route tokens for enterprise. Start with tenant-level for pilot.

carla (eng): runtime implications: need a token-check in the router path + accounting hook. Low-latency checks ok, but we need atomic decrement and audit logs. implementation estimate: 2 sprints for pilot pattern + metrics.

yuki (devex): SDK/API: expose a header x-redwood-priority-token (or boolean) and a CLI for token balance. docs + example flows needed. we'll need example SDK snippet and tests showing token consumption.

oliver (finance): pricing model thoughts: subscription $99/mo + token pack (e.g., 100k priority tokens = $250). Need to model gross margin with reserved capacity for priority lane. Also cap for token rollover?

frank (ops): ops note: priority lane requires either small soft reserve or prioritized queue (no hard reserves initially). For pilot we can do prioritized queue. If tokens drive SLA promises, ops will ask for committed capacity SKU.

sue (legal): contract concerns: we need clear language on what tokens guarantee and carveouts for safety/regulatory. Draft clause: ```Priority Tokens grant Customer prioritized routing for requests that present valid tokens. Priority is relative and not an absolute latency SLA. Redwood may adjust routing during capacity stress or for safety reasons. Tokens do not guarantee identical model outputs.``` Need definitions for "prioritized" and "capacity stress."

maya (pm): launch criteria proposed: 1) router+token accounting working in staging, 2) docs+SDK sample, 3) sales pilot with 3 customers, 4) contract clause agreed, 5) monitoring: token burn-rate and 99th latency for priority vs baseline.

anya (pm): also add eval requirement: priority path quality should not degrade >3% on our canonical prompts vs default path. we should define the prompts.

dan (sales): pilot ask: can we give first pack free for 30 days? customers like risk-free trials. Also, can tokens be gifted to trials and tracked in billing?

oliver (finance): free trial tokens OK for pilot. For billing we need visibility into token redemption events to reconcile invoicing and revenue recognition. plan to add token usage export to billing pipeline.

carla (eng): telemetry: will emit token.events with fields (tenant, route, token_id, timestamp) to BigQuery. also emit a daily aggregated burn report. That supports finance and ops.

frank (ops): for pilot we'll host priority queue in us-east-1 only. scaling to multi-region is phase 2. need QPS estimate from sales by EOD Fri.

yuki (devex): I'll draft quickstart + sample code. Suggested example: ```client = Redwood(api_key)
client.request(prompt, priority_token=True)
``` plus a local script to simulate token exhaustion.

sue (legal): added: also include a change-control clause allowing Redwood to modify priority behavior with X days notice if safety/regulatory reasons arise.

oliver (finance): request: show three sensitivity scenarios (low/med/high adoption) and impact on unit margin. I'll model subscription + token revenue vs ops cost.

maya (pm): owners: maya (PM), carla (eng), dan (sales), yuki (devex), oliver (finance), sue (legal), frank (ops). Pilot scope decisions: - tenant-level tokens, - US-only, - 3 pilot customers for 30 days, - free starter pack.

anya (pm): timeline check: can we go live pilot in 5 weeks? engineering + ops dependency.

carla (eng): 5 weeks doable if scope stays US-only and we do prioritized queue instead of hard reserves.

dan (sales): I'll line up customers and ask for their spike windows.

sue (legal): will prepare simple addendum for trial + priority token T&Cs.

yuki (devex): will prepare quickstart + an eval harness to measure quality delta.

maya (pm): ok locking this. If any vetoes, raise now. Otherwise I'll post MRD + rollout checklist by Tue.

frank (ops): no veto. will confirm infra ETA after QPS input.

oliver (finance): no veto; will deliver models.

sue (legal): will post redlines tomorrow.

yuki (devex): working on docs.

anya (pm): thumbs up. Scheduling kickoff next Tue 9am PT.

maya (pm): thanks all. We'll track action items in the MRD and link pilot customers once confirmed.
